The hiphil of יסף, add, is rendered by the comparative more.

The second כֹּה takes also: the oath formula's three morphemes (waw, כֹּה, יוֹסִיף) answer to the three English words and, more, also, so counting them against each other under rule 42's reasoning leaves no surplus on either side. The competing reading marks כֹּה unrepresented and also added.
Oath אִם לֹא written out as if ... not by the ASV, so rule 30's one-English-word condition for the surely fusion is unmet and rule 2 splits the pair.
Verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17), headed on the verb (rule 24).
The negative half of the split oath formula (see the אִם above).
Construct noun takes only its own English (rule 19).
Nomen rectum takes the of-expression (rule 19); no article morpheme stands in the chain, so the supplied the belongs to the nominal expression and stands before host (rules 15, 29).

לִפְנֵי rendered by the single English word before: rule 30 fusion, headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme. Recorded noncompositional, as the same fusion is at 2SA.19.8, 2SA.19.17 and 2SA.19.18; the corpus reads this expression both ways, so the chapter convention decides it.
Suffix as object pronoun of the compound preposition (rule 18).

כָּל־הַיָּמִים rendered by the one English word continually, so the three morphemes share a unit (rule 30). Head on יָּמִים as the morpheme carrying the durative lexeme; heading on כֹּל is defensible since the totality is part of what continually says.

תַּחַת rendered by the compound preposition in the room of, a single rendering no morpheme owns a part of (rule 30); one source morpheme, so the unit is aligned rather than a fusion, and the head goes to the lexeme-bearing token rather than a connective (rule 24).
Proper name.

review_notes: Only the status of the לְפָנַי and כָּל־הַיָּמִים units changed; their edges and heads are as the verse pass returned them, and no other unit was touched.
Every source and target ID is partitioned exactly once; this verse has no added and no unrepresented units.
The fronted Art stays on the interrogative הֲ rather than being read as rule 20's construction-supplied copula, following rule 17; the explicit אַתָּה keeps only thou.
